title: A Grassmann proof of the Catalan divisor in the Teufl–Wagner forest transfer determinant
verdict: PASS — all-n integral Catalan divisor in the full Bell-space normalization

initial.assessment: Complete native article read. Independently reconstructed tree-basis wedge, paired extraction, Catalan invariant span and character, and ordered Gaussian factorization.

proof: Orientation and basis changes in each forest block square the unimodular determinant. Cycle wedges vanish. In the edge-subset exponential each subset has coefficient one. If any component has no Y vertex it lacks top X degree. Otherwise star replacement at a Y root leaves a unique positive top paired coefficient and the correct output forest-state vector.

Weight subtraction computes invariant dimensions. Noncrossing perfect matchings have distinct leading Dyck words and number C_r; tensor invariants generate exterior ones by equivariant antisymmetrization. Bilinear degree-two generators decompose into q edge factors. Vandermonde gives C_n, and degree symmetry plus torus weights and permutation conjugacy give determinant character (det g)^C_n.

Gaussian completion uses the specified factor order, namely degree-lowering normalization, B preserving the mean-zero coefficient space, and degree-raising symmetric zero-sum S. Only the middle determinant plus detD scalar remains, giving exactly (det A)^C_n without numerical row-sum assumptions. The constant quotient permits a rational constant block decomposition of T transpose; multivariate Gauss lemma upgrades the divisor to Z. n=1 is explicit.
primary: Actual pp.1457–1458 identify full Bell partition set, arbitrary fixed block trees, each interlayer subset once, and Catalan question.

reproduction.method: Independent explicit weighted edge-subset enumeration with exact rational elimination, star and path input trees; signed, singular and zero-row-sum controls. No third-party source or archive computation needed for these finite checks.

independent.verdict: PASS. Independent complete proof, source interfaces, all native pages, and static support. Historical graph comparator has documented ordinary-Python assertion-side-effect limitation.

limits: The conclusion is an integral divisor. Exact multiplicity, complete factorization, historical firstness and independent discovery are not certified.

follow_up.question: For every n≥9, is det A absent as a factor of det T/(det A)^C_n?
follow_up.why: Equivalent to asking whether the constant-kernel block remains invertible at a generic rank-(n−1) specialization. A resolution would determine the exact order of vanishing along the singular-matrix divisor and whether the Catalan quotient accounts for its full multiplicity.
follow_up.credit: Ferudun §7.4 asks the all-n exactness question and reports verification through n=8. Bounded primary search did not identify a general theorem. No worldwide-open claim.
